//: EXAMPLE configuration - placeholder values only. Copy this to appsettings.Production.json in
the service directory on the server (DEPLOYMENT.md step 9) and fill in the real values there.
This file is committed so the SHAPE of the configuration is documented. The real file lives
outside the repository, is owned root:crt-server at mode 0640, and must never be copied back
in - .gitignore blocks appsettings.Production.json for that reason.
Every value under DataTreeRoot, ProductionTreeRoot, PublicDataBaseUrl, ManifestPath,
ConnectionString and PublicApiBaseUrl has NO DEFAULT in code. A missing or malformed one
stops the service from starting, with the offending setting named in the journal. That is
deliberate: the failure mode of forgetting is an outage, not a service quietly writing data

CrtServer.//DataTreeRoot: The BETA tree the service may write. On this server: /mydir/http/classic-repair-toolbox.dk/public_html/app-data-BETA/Data
CrtServer.//ProductionTreeRoot: Named ONLY so it can be refused. The service never writes it - promotion is a manual copy. The real guarantee is that the service user has no write permission there (DEPLOYMENT.md step 3); this is the in-code half.
CrtServer.//RequiredTreeMarker: Every configured path and the public data URL must contain this. Clear it ONLY when deliberately targeting a tree without it.
CrtServer.//PublicDataBaseUrl: Becomes the url of every entry in dataChecksums.json (Phase 5). Pairing the BETA tree with the production URL yields a valid manifest that sends every client to the wrong data, which is why this is validated from Phase 3 even though nothing reads it yet.
CrtServer.//ManifestPath: Where dataChecksums.json is written. It sits BESIDE the data root, not inside it, so it cannot be derived from DataTreeRoot.
CrtServer.//BlobStoreRoot: Where submitted files are stored, content-addressed by SHA-256 (Phase 4). MUST be an absolute path OUTSIDE the web document root - blobs of a submission still under review would otherwise be downloadable by anyone who guessed a hash. Put it beside the service, e.g. <site>/crt-server/blobs. It accumulates contributor-supplied bytes, so watch its size.
CrtServer.//ConnectionString: MariaDB. Create a dedicated user; do not reuse another application's credentials.
CrtServer.//PublicApiBaseUrl: Builds the links in verification and password-reset mail. Must be https.
CrtServer.//Smtp: Local postfix. No authentication and no TLS: the connection never leaves the box, and postfix handles outbound delivery. MailFromAddress is REQUIRED from the accounts step - mail sent without a From address is rejected by the receiving server, and a missing one would fail when somebody registers rather than at startup.
CrtServer.//Tokens: Access is short because it is presented on every request; refresh is long because this audience opens CRT every few weeks, and forcing frequent password re-entry trains people into weaker passwords.
CrtServer.//Argon2: RFC 9106's second recommended profile, sized for a small box. May be RAISED without invalidating existing passwords - the encoded hash carries the parameters it was made with. The validator refuses to start below a floor, so these cannot be quietly weakened.
